_about: Owner-approved specs for the road to early access (docs/ROADMAP.md). Each spec stays passes:false until its test passes in a place drawn at random from all 56 AND the finisher has played it in the test bench. Sessions may change only 'passes' (with evidence in the PR). They may never edit 'test'. The CTO adds 'command' once a spec's automated test exists. M1 to M7 specs are added here when the owner approves them. M2-01 sits under M1 because the owner moved it there (built with M1-12 in M1-officials).

milestones.M0: Foundation and the test bench (owner-approved Oct 10, 2026)
milestones.M2: Running for office (owner-approved piece by piece from Oct 12, 2026)

features.title: The bench opens in a Codespace
features.test: Three different seeds give three different places in three different states or territories; each builds without error; and every resident on the list exists in the core's records.

features.title: Play anyone
features.test: Over 7 days, every act on the chosen person's record came from a choice made on screen, other residents' lives continue, and choosing an option nobody offered is impossible.

features.title: Time: Day, Week, Calendar, and skip until something needs you
features.test: A skip from a random date stops exactly at the earliest of: a moment at or over the 0.50 interrupt line, a fixed commitment, or an offer with a deadline; it says which one; nothing was skipped past.

features.title: Click anything, see why
features.test: 20 randomly sampled items on screen each open a 'why' with scores and record ids that exist in the core; none is made up for display.

features.title: The golden path and world panel
features.test: For a fresh life, steps 1-2 show reachable, steps 3-11 show the specific missing module, and the world pieces show 'not in the new core yet' until M1 lands.

features.title: Step 1: a life at 18
features.test: In a random place, the 18-year-old's parents and siblings follow the kin rules; schools are real schools from the place data (real naming patterns where none exists); every fact shown has a record behind it.

features.title: Step 2: meeting people
features.test: Over 91 days in a random place: the player gains new acquaintances through real encounters, at least one grows closer, and visits to parents and siblings fall inside the survey ranges (GSS, ATUS); over years, circle turnover matches a sourced study.

features.title: Money that works for a year
features.test: A full year in a random place: under 10% of businesses close; sales pay more than half of all wages; every dollar balances; outside money is reported next to real public spending and Social Security per resident; national conditions flat and labeled until M1.

features.title: The four core pieces
features.test: Module state, accounts with one balanced writer, the institution calendar and voter groups each have their own contract tests; the speed budget holds; the first two M1 ports build on them without patching the core.

features.title: The golden-path test suite runs on every change
features.test: A deliberately broken step-2 change turns the check red, and the suite fits its time budget.

features.title: Speed and memory guard
features.test: A change that makes a year more than 20% slower than its base fails the check, and the report names the slowest steps.

features.title: Feature list and progress file
features.test: A fresh session can read docs/roadmap/features.json and docs/roadmap/PROGRESS.md, pick the top unfinished feature and start without asking anyone what's next.

features.title: Laws in force, every level
features.test: For a random place, tracked laws (minimum wage; income, sales and property taxes; major benefit amounts) match that place's real starting law at every level; a higher level's override wins where it legally does; a law that hasn't taken effect yet doesn't apply.

features.title: The national economy and central bank
features.test: A one-year run keeps national figures within real historical spreads (each month's 12-month change in unemployment, prices and payroll jobs, and each quarter's output growth, inside the 5th to 95th percentile of 1990 to the latest year); a rate decision changes what loans cost in the town; every decision is traceable to the members' reasons, with no random draws.

features.title: State and metro economies
features.test: In a year, two randomly drawn states diverge plausibly in jobs and wages (each inside the real spread of one-year state changes since 2000); a town's prices and pay follow its region; each state's and metro's starting figures match real data.

features.title: Jobs
features.test: Over a year in a random place, unemployment, hiring and quitting stay within real ranges (federal job-turnover data), and every job change on record has a reason.

features.title: Housing
features.test: Rents and home prices in a random place fall within real ranges for its region; an eviction happens only from unpaid rent, through the steps that place's law requires.

features.title: Credit and banks
features.test: Every loan's money balances from lender to borrower and back; defaults follow borrowers' real circumstances, never a chance roll.

features.title: Budgets and taxes, every level
features.test: In a random place over a year, every level adopts a budget on its real calendar; federal and state money reaches named residents and the town; every dollar balances; spending and taxes per resident fall within real ranges.

features.title: Businesses grow and shrink
features.test: A year's business openings and closings stay within real rates (Census Business Dynamics Statistics); owners' income comes from profit; across multi-year runs, some businesses add locations without being scripted to.

features.title: Births, moves and new residents
features.test: A year's births and moves in a random place stay within that place's real rates; the town's population changes the way real towns do instead of winding down.

features.title: Political views
features.test: In a random place, views match real spreads by age, education, faith and region, checked against state and metro answer keys, so conservatives in two randomly drawn states can differ; a big event shifts the people it touches and no one else.

features.title: Drives answer the economy
features.test: Over a year, job losses, evictions and closures form drives at a researched rate, and a drive's target is a real person or institution involved in the event.

features.title: Important people everywhere
features.test: Click any official in any state: a full record with personality, history, relationships and the positions behind their votes.

features.title: Offices and seats, every level
features.test: In a random place, every seat that covers the player has a holder with a record and a term; a vacancy is filled the way that office's real rules say.

features.title: Other places, coarser
features.test: In a year, other places' populations and voters' views change from their own conditions within real ranges, and their public events are recorded with place and date so news (M2-09) can carry them. (Narrowed by the owner, Oct 10: other councils legislating is M3-10; news delivery is M2-09.)

features.title: History before your start
features.test: A new game in a random place opens on its start date; people have recent life events dated in the years before it; the economy's recent path matches real figures; laws in force show their dated changes before the start; governments show prior years' budgets; the load time and size are measured. (Owner, Oct 10: officials' election records and recent laws with their effects are added with M2 and M3.)

features.title: Election calendars and filing rules
features.test: In a random place, the next local, state and federal elections have that place's real dates, and filing requires exactly what that place's rules require (age, residency, registration, a fee or signatures), read from data.

features.title: Filing in person
features.test: In a random place, the player goes to that place's real filing office, talks to the person there through dialogue choices, picks an office in the filing overlay, states a platform, gathers any required signatures from real people, files once and is on the ballot; an ineligible player is told the rule in words.

features.title: Campaigning
features.test: In a random place, after filing, each campaign activity (doors, volunteers, fundraising within real contribution limits, events and speeches, ads, endorsements, staff) changes what specific people know and think, each change with a recorded cause; support never moves without one; rivals campaign with the same tools.

features.title: Polls
features.test: In a random place, a poll reports what the people it actually contacted told the pollster (including undecided and no opinion), with a computed margin of error; no contacts means no poll; true support is never shown on screen.
